You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: What image-grounded evidence, if any, establishes progress on relocating the requested mug to the headphones' right?
node.criteria: pass: Visible evidence establishes some requested relocation progress; describe the concrete change and whether it establishes an incomplete or completed result. fail: The images establish no requested relocation progress, such as the identifiable target remaining unchanged while only unrelated objects or scene details change. unknown: The evidence cannot distinguish requested progress from unrelated changes or ambiguous object correspondence. Neither a change of any kind nor a right-side unidentified mug alone establishes progress. Do not require a reconstructed editing operation or a particular trajectory.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images directly, tracking the requested source mug using multiple visible features and scene correspondence. Assess progress toward the requested relative placement rather than arbitrary displacement. Distinguish evidence of relocation from uncertain disappearance, added objects, and appearance changes; these possibilities are hypotheses, not predetermined findings. Inspect independently even if endpoint correspondence is unresolved, and report any independently grounded progress evidence without inventing continuity.

node_traces.evidence: The source has one distinctive light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, that mug is not clearly identifiable: there is a blue blurred shape at the left and two small white mugs, with no reliable visual correspondence establishing that the source mug was relocated to the headphones’ right. The apparent changes therefore do not establish requested relocation progress.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too generic to preserve target identity: the source mug is specifically the large light-blue mug with a curved handle, initially left of the black headphones. Make the binding explicitly compare that source object across the before/after images, rather than treating any mug on the headphones’ right as the target. The edited image shows two small pale mugs, headphones, and a blurred blue shape at far left; neither support establishes which, if either, is the original mug. Do not infer progress or completion from the right-side mug alone, but ensure the criterion can recognize independently grounded partial relocation if evidence establishes it. Keep unresolved identity unresolved when visual correspondence is genuinely insufficient. The trace is valid uncertainty, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; the reference label “partial” is an aggregate constraint, not proof of a particular mug’s identity or progress.
